Let me analyze the Dafny verification failure.

The errors are:
1. `program.dfy(70,7): Error: Verification of 'InsertBST' timed out after 25 seconds.`
2. `program.dfy(205,0): Error: a postcondition could not be proved on this return path`
3. `program.dfy(204,9): Related location: this is the postcondition that could not be proved`

Looking at line 204-205, this is the `lemma_all_small`:

```dafny
lemma {:verify true} lemma_all_small(q:seq<int>,i:int)
	requires forall k:: 0 <= k < |q| ==> q[k] in NumbersInSequence(q)
	ensures forall j::0<=j < |q| ==> q[j] < i
{}
```

The postcondition `forall j::0<=j < |q| ==> q[j] < i` is clearly NOT implied by the precondition `forall k:: 0 <= k < |q| ==> q[k] in NumbersInSequence(q)`. 

The precondition just says every element of q is in the set of elements of q (which is trivially true and says nothing about bounds). The postcondition requires every element to be less than `i`. These are completely unrelated - the precondition doesn't give any information about the values being less than `i`.

The counterexample confirms this: `i = 0, q[22] = 7719, q[38] = 7719, |q| = 39`. So the elements are 7719 which is NOT less than 0, but the precondition is still satisfied (elements are in the set of elements).

The intended purpose of `lemma_all_small` is to help prove that all elements in a sequence are less than some value `i`. Looking at the context where it's used:

```dafny
assert forall j :: j in NumbersInSequence(new_left_nums) ==> j < i;
assert forall j :: j in NumbersInSequence(new_left_nums) <==> j in new_left_nums;

assert forall j,k::0<=j < k < |new_left_nums| ==> new_left_nums[j] < new_left_nums[k];
assert x < i;
lemma_all_small(new_left_nums,i);
assert forall j::0<=j < |new_left_nums| ==> new_left_nums[j] < i;
```

The intent is: if all elements in the sequence are in the set that are all less than `i`, then each element is less than `i`. The precondition should be about the elements being less than `i` in the set sense, not just being in the set.

The correct precondition should be: `forall k :: k in NumbersInSequence(q) ==> k < i`

This would make the lemma say: if all elements in the set of q are less than i, and each q[j] is in NumbersInSequence(q), then q[j] < i.

Looking at `lemma_all_big`:
```dafny

	requires forall k:: 0 <= k < |q| ==> q[k] in NumbersInSequence(q)
	ensures forall j::0<=j < |q| ==> q[j] > i
{}
```

This one has the correct structure - it requires that all elements in the set are > i, and that each q[k] is in the set. Then it concludes q[j] > i.

So `lemma_all_small` should have a similar structure:
```dafny
lemma lemma_all_small(q:seq<int>,i:int)
	requires forall k:: k in NumbersInSequence(q) ==> k < i
	requires forall k:: 0 <= k < |q| ==> q[k] in NumbersInSequence(q)
	ensures forall j::0<=j < |q| ==> q[j] < i
{}
```

The missing precondition is `forall k:: k in NumbersInSequence(q) ==> k < i`.
